label: Edison's tinfoil phonograph
detail: The first machine to record and play back sound; patent application filed December 24, 1877.

label: Berliner patents the gramophone
detail: Flat, double-sided discs with spiral grooves, cheaper to mass-produce than cylinders.

label: Commercial shellac 78s begin
detail: Shellac discs are produced commercially from 1897 until the late 1950s.

label: Edison switches to discs
detail: Edison announces the Edison Disc Phonograph, conceding the public prefers discs; cylinders continue until 1929.

label: Columbia unveils the LP
detail: Announced at the Waldorf Astoria in New York; the Library of Congress gives June 21, other sources June 18.

label: RCA Victor introduces the 45
detail: A 7-inch 45 rpm single with a large center hole, the day after Columbia announced a 7-inch 33 1/3 single.

label: The war of the speeds ends in a split
detail: RCA issues LPs in April and Columbia issues 45s in August: LP for albums, 45 for singles.

label: RIAA curve approved
detail: The RIAA Technical Committee approves one US playback equalization standard, still in use.

label: Stereo standard adopted
detail: The RIAA adopts the Westrex 45/45 single-groove stereo system as the US standard.

label: Cassettes pass LPs
detail: Cassettes take 47.8% of US dollar value against 44.6% for LPs and EPs.

label: US vinyl hits bottom
detail: RIAA LP and EP shipments fall to about 900,000 (SoundScan's low, 857,000 albums, came in 2005).

label: First Record Store Day
detail: Conceived in September 2007 and first held in April 2008.

label: US vinyl revenue passes CD
detail: $626 million against $483 million, the first time since 1986 (RIAA).

label: US vinyl passes CD in units
detail: 41 million vinyl units against 33 million CDs, the first time since 1987 (RIAA).

label: US vinyl tops $1 billion
detail: $1,042.9 million on 46.8 million units, the 19th straight year of growth (RIAA).
